title: Kenyan Waffles with Mango
community: Urban Kenya — the hotel weekend brunch
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Waffles with Mango — crispy Belgian-style waffles topped with fresh mango slices, passion fruit pulp, coconut whipped cream, and a drizzle of Kenyan honey. The weekend hotel brunch treat that celebrates what Kenya does best.
longDesc: Waffles have taken root in Nairobi's hotel brunch culture — and the Kenyan version, topped with local mango and passion fruit rather than imported maple syrup, is genuinely superior to the standard presentation.
ingredients: 200ml coconut cream — whipped with 1 tbsp honey
steps: Separate eggs. Beat egg whites to stiff peaks.
Mix egg yolks, milk, oil, and vanilla.
Combine flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt.
Mix wet into dry until just combined.
Fold egg whites into batter — do not deflate.
Cook waffles until golden and crispy — follow manufacturer timing.
Whip coconut cream with honey to soft peaks.
Top waffles with coconut cream, mango, passion fruit, and honey drizzle.
chefTips: Folding beaten egg whites into the batter is the secret to crispy, light waffles.
Do not open the waffle iron early — it tears the waffle.
Serve immediately — waffles lose crispiness quickly.
commonMistakes: Not folding egg whites — dense waffles.
cookingScience: The whipped egg whites in the batter create a foam structure that expands in the hot waffle iron — creating the characteristic light interior. The oil in the batter prevents the waffle from sticking and contributes to the crispy exterior by limiting steam retention on the surface.
sustainabilityTips: Coconut cream, mango, passion fruit, and honey — all locally produced in Kenya.
healthBenefits: Mango provides vitamins A and C.
Best enjoyed as a brunch treat.
culturalNote: Kenyan waffles with mango represent the modernisation of the Kenyan hotel breakfast — a globally familiar format made extraordinary by the quality of Kenya's tropical fruit and the depth of its wild honey.
